title: Embedding a free rational Lie algebra into its associative word algebra
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set and let $F(I)$ be a free rational Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra] on generators $z_i$: every assignment of the $z_i$ to a rational Lie algebra extends uniquely to a Lie homomorphism. Let $A(I)$ be the unital associative rational algebra whose vector-space basis consists of all finite words in $I$, including the empty word $1$, and whose multiplication is concatenation. Write $t_i$ for the one-letter word $i$, and give $A(I)$ the Lie bracket $[a,b]=ab-ba$. The unique Lie homomorphism
$$q:F(I)\longrightarrow A(I),\qquad q(z_i)=t_i,$$
is injective. The empty generating set is allowed.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504, supporting free-Lie input to the asserted freeness of the two subalgebras. The embedding lemma is supplied by the agent, not proved in Milne; WANTED: Bourbaki, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Chapters 1--3, Chapter II, free Lie algebras and their embedding into tensor algebras. Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/Free.lean:36--44 and SerreConstruction.lean:40--46 describe precisely this missing identification.

proof.text: Put $F=F(I)$ and form $U=U(F)$ with canonical linear map $j:F\to U$ using [lem-sfb-enveloping-universal-property]. By [lem-sfb-arbitrary-basis-pbw], $j$ is injective; this theorem applies to every rational Lie algebra, so no finite-dimensionality assumption on $F$ is needed. The defining quotient relation gives $j([x,y])=j(x)j(y)-j(y)j(x)$ for every $x,y\in F$, hence $j$ is a Lie homomorphism into the commutator Lie algebra of $U$.

source.place: Section 10j, pp.199–200, Theorem 10.36; supporting the free-Lie assertion of Theorem 23.63, first proof, p.504.

proof.text: Define a rational linear map $p:A(I)\to U$ on the given word basis by $p(1)=1$ and $p(t_{i_1}\cdots t_{i_n})=j(z_{i_1})\cdots j(z_{i_n})$. Every element of $A(I)$ is a finite linear combination of words, so this specifies $p$ uniquely. On two basis words, concatenation and associativity in $U$ give $p(vw)=p(v)p(w)$, including empty words. Bilinearity extends this equality to arbitrary elements. Thus $p$ is a unital rational algebra homomorphism and $p([a,b])=p(ab-ba)=p(a)p(b)-p(b)p(a)$, so it is also a Lie homomorphism.

source.place: Section 10j, pp.199–200, Theorem 10.36; supporting the free-Lie assertion of Theorem 23.63, first proof, p.504.

proof.text: The Lie homomorphisms $p\circ q$ and $j$ from $F(I)$ to $U$ have the same value $j(z_i)$ on each generator. The uniqueness clause in the stated universal property of $F(I)$ gives $p\circ q=j$. If $q(x)=q(y)$, applying $p$ gives $j(x)=j(y)$, and the injectivity obtained in step 1 gives $x=y$. This proves injectivity of $q$. All constructions allow $I=\varnothing$; moreover in that case the identity and zero Lie endomorphisms of $F(I)$ agree by the same uniqueness clause, so $F(I)=0$, and the assertion is the injectivity of $0\to\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Section 10j, pp.199–200, Theorem 10.36; supporting the free-Lie assertion of Theorem 23.63, first proof, p.504.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 10.36 and the construction of U(L), pp.199–200, followed by the explicit word-evaluation argument and uniqueness in the free Lie universal property; used for Theorem 23.63, p.504.
